# Shared-endpoint circuit credits without centroid alignment

Research draft, 6 November 2026. This is an unconditional cap-payment lemma for actual fibers. It does not assert that its credits are universally positive or sufficiently numerous to settle OC.

Let C be a convex body in R^n x R^d, d>=1. Fix a middle integer base w and a point y in its actual fiber K_w. Let p_j, j in J, be distinct integer outer bases with positive-volume fibers A_j, and let z_i, i in I, be distinct integer bases with full-dimensional fibers C_i. Assume the three groups {w}, {p_j}, {z_i} are pairwise disjoint, but allow the same high endpoint z_i to be used in many different relations. Put

    E=sum_j |A_j|>0, and suppose E<=min_i |C_i|.           (1)

For each j suppose there are numbers beta_j>0 and lambda_ji>=0 with

    beta_j+sum_i lambda_ji=1,
    beta_j p_j+sum_i lambda_ji z_i=w.                     (2)

The lambda coefficients may be zero, so each small fiber can have its own circuit support. No relation between the continuous centroids is assumed.

For any nonconstant affine functional f on R^d, define

    r_i=(E/|C_i|)^{1/d},
    q_i(f)=max_{C_i}f-r_i(max_{C_i}f-min_{C_i}f),
    Q_j(f,y)={x in A_j:
           beta_j f(x)+sum_i lambda_ji q_i(f)>=f(y)},
    c(f,y)=sum_j |Q_j(f,y)|.                              (3)

Then every closed ambient halfspace through (w,y) with continuous normal a positive multiple of the oriented gradient of f has endpoint contribution at least c(f,y):

    sum_i |C_i intersect H_{z_i}|
       +sum_j |A_j intersect H_{p_j}|
          >= c(f,y).                                    (4)

In particular its total source mass is at least |K_w intersect H_w|+c(f,y). The credits in (3) are independent of the integer part of the halfspace normal.

Proof. Write the halfspace as u dot (z-w)+f(x)-f(y)>=0. Its threshold in a fiber at base z is tau_z=f(y)-u dot(z-w). Equation (2) gives the exact scalar cancellation

    beta_j tau_{p_j}+sum_i lambda_ji tau_{z_i}=f(y).       (5)

For each high fiber C_i, choose a point attaining max f and take the homothetic copy of C_i about it with ratio r_i. Condition (1) ensures 0<r_i<=1. This copy lies in C_i, has volume exactly E, and lies in {f>=q_i(f)}. Therefore if any one high endpoint has cap mass at least E, it alone pays (4), since c(f,y)<=sum_j|A_j|=E.

In the remaining case every high endpoint cap has mass less than E. The preceding homothetic witness forces tau_{z_i}>q_i(f) for every i. For a fixed j, (5) then gives

    beta_j tau_{p_j}
       <= f(y)-sum_i lambda_ji q_i(f),                    (6)

with strict inequality whenever at least one lambda_ji>0. Such a positive coefficient must exist: otherwise beta_j=1 and (2) would give p_j=w, excluded by distinctness. Hence (6) is strict. Every x in Q_j(f,y) therefore satisfies f(x)>tau_{p_j}, and belongs to the actual closed cap at p_j. Summing the distinct small-fiber caps gives at least c(f,y), proving (4).

The argument counts each high endpoint only once, even if it appears in many rows of (2). This is legal because its cap budget is the **total** E, not one row's mass. It also counts each outer fiber exactly once. The alternative in the proof is global: either one high cap pays all credits, or every high threshold is beyond its E-volume witness and each tiny fiber pays its own assigned credit. There is no fictitious independent resampling of a shared endpoint.

If f is constant (a purely integer halfspace), the entire middle fiber is present. To combine the lemma with a proposed target bound T, one must separately check T<=|K_w|; this note does not assume it automatically.

## Normalization and possible combination with local repair

An arbitrary common affine change in the continuous coordinates transforms every support value and halfspace consistently; no separate global translation of individual actual fibers is being performed. Opposite or weighted translations of the endpoint bodies can be used only as a calculation if they preserve the cancellation sum in (2) and the thresholds in (5). Formula (3) already avoids needing such translations.

For near-simplex middle fibers, a local displacement argument could use fixed subsets of the Q_j in neighborhoods of the simplex's critical facet directions, provided a proved geometric condition supplies uniform incidence and a positive margin in (3). The errors arising from the r_i are controlled by E/min_i|C_i| and do not depend on the number of circuits. Establishing the necessary facet incidence for arbitrary unaligned endpoint bodies remains additional work; it is not claimed here.

This lemma generalizes the one-partner cap-payment step in pending `ff31d56304dd901a`: beta_j=lambda_j=1/2, one partner per row. The new distinction is that arbitrarily many higher-arity rows may share actual high endpoint fibers while remaining a valid source-mass bound. Its cost is the total-volume quantile E at every reused high endpoint.
